document_title: The Anchorage Paper That Wrote Itself, Then Stopped
post_copy:
Daily, at a site called The Daily Anchorage, means July 8th to July 26th.
Nothing since. More than 500 stories are still live on August 13th.

The form is all there. Politics, property, schools, transport. A corrections page and legal notices. No named reporter appears anywhere.

Bylines go to desks. Each article checked says it "was not reviewed by a journalist before publishing."

The about page promises to disclose AI involvement on every page, and it does. It asks readers to verify anything important.

The deck sets the tagline against the dates and lists the network's 18 mastheads, all Australian. Anchorage is not one.

Every part of a newsroom is here except the part that does the reporting.

Does full disclosure earn a page the word local, or does that still need a person who can be asked about the story?

#AlaskaMedia #NewsDeserts #AIDisclosure

aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8am to 11am Alaska time.
Paste the first comment immediately, inside the first minute, so the sources land with the post.
Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. Threaded author replies are the strongest reach lever this page has.
If a commenter asks whether the site is illegal, the honest answer is that it disclosed and Alaska has no law on this. That is the deck's point.
Do not name the founder in replies. The deck deliberately carries the absence of a registered legal entity instead.
Do not link the site in a comment. Describing it is enough and a link rewards it.
editor_notes_for_email:
The deck is built entirely on the publisher's own printed words, which is why it can be this direct without being an accusation. Slide 3 is the fairness beat and it is load-bearing. It credits the site for disclosing truthfully and shows, in the art, that the review it promised was for flagged content only.

Two numbers are deliberately soft and the softness is printed on the slides. The sitemap would not count the same way three times running, so the deck says more than 500. Public Citizen's tracker read 33 states once and 23 another time, so the deck says more than 20 and draws the row open. Both are floors, not estimates.

The August 18th primary appears on slide 8 as timing only, with the guard printed on the slide itself in the deck's own voice rather than hidden in a footnote. There is no evidence linking this site to the election and the deck says so out loud.

One thing the scouts offered that did NOT survive. A doctored image of a gubernatorial candidate was reported to be circulating. The fact-checker searched the outlet twice, found 61 results in strict date order with a clean gap across the claimed publication date, and could not find it. Nothing about it is in this deck.
